settings.headline: The dry-eye symptom no one warned you about at 40+
settings.author: The Dewy Team
settings.lead: If your eyes feel gritty by mid-afternoon, sting at the computer, and water for no reason — and every drop you've tried wears off within the hour — here's the mechanism behind it, and the simplest first step that actually helps.
settings.hero_caption: The Dewy Cooling & Warming Gel Eye Mask
settings.agitate_title: Why it gets worse in your 40s and 50s
settings.agitate_body:
Here's the part most people never get told: the tiny glands along your eyelid rims — the ones that make the oily top layer of your tears — start to clog and slow down as we age, and the hormonal shifts of perimenopause speed that up. Less oil means your tears evaporate before they can do their job. That's why the drops feel great for an hour and then you're gritty again: they top up the water, but they can't fix the oil.

It's not in your head, and it's not just "getting older." It's a specific, well-understood mechanism — and it responds to a specific, well-understood first step.
settings.pullquote: Warm-compress therapy is named a first-line treatment for evaporative dry eye in the international TFOS DEWS II consensus — the reference eye specialists actually use.
settings.mech_intro: Dewy is a warm and cold compress mask designed around the one thing that matters for this: gentle, even temperature held long enough to do something.
settings.mech1_title: Warms the oil so it can flow again
settings.mech1_body: Research indicates the eyelid needs to reach around 40°C to soften the thickened oils blocking the glands. Dewy is built to hold a comfortable, even warmth across the whole lid — not a towel that's scalding then cold in 90 seconds.
settings.mech2_body: The reason warm compresses fail people isn't the science — it's that a hot flannel is annoying, so nobody keeps it up. Dewy is a 10-minute routine you'll actually do, which is the whole game with this.
settings.mech3_title: Reusable, and made to feel like a ritual
settings.mech3_body: Soft, washable, and calming enough that it becomes the nice part of your evening rather than a chore. That's deliberate — comfort is what makes it a habit.
settings.evidence_body:
We won't tell you Dewy is a cure or a replacement for anything your optometrist has given you — it isn't, and anyone claiming that about a mask is being dishonest with you.

What's true: warm-compress and lid-warming therapy is recognised as a first-line approach for evaporative dry eye and meibomian gland dysfunction by the international TFOS DEWS II report and recommended by major eye-care bodies including the American Optometric Association and American Academy of Ophthalmology. Meibomian gland dysfunction is the leading cause of dry eye. A warm compress is one of the simplest, best-evidenced first steps you can take at home — often used alongside the care your eye professional gives you.

The honest framing: not a miracle, just the sensible, specialist-backed first thing to try — done in a way you'll actually stick to.
